newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Croatia FinMin sees growth up, inflation steady.
newsitem.headline: Croatia FinMin sees growth up, inflation steady.

text.p: Croatian Finance Minister Bozo Prka said on Thursday he expected the country's economy to expand by up to seven percent this year, while latest data showed inflation to be steady at around 3.5 percent.
"Croatia's economic growth will be at about the same level as last year, that is between six and seven percent," Prka told a news briefing in Vienna.
He added inflation was currently running at an annual 3.5 percent, while industrial production -- accounting for about a third of gross domestic product -- had grown by some 5.5 percent in March.
"Croatia continues on the path of stability and growth," Prka said.
The minister added that local elections held earlier this month had paved the way to re-establishing Croatian control over Serb-held Eastern Slavonia, which is now under U.N. mandate.
"There is no doubt that Eastern Slavonia will be peacefully reintegrated by the end of June," he said. "The elections went very smoothly."
Former rebel Serbs won 11 of 29 municipalities in Eastern Slavonia, while unofficial results showed that Croatian parties captured a narrow majority in the key city of Vukovar.
Prka said the election results should help improve Croatia's overall economic performance and increase its chances to raise its profile on the world's capital markets.

"After these elections Croatia has confirmed itself as a peaceful country, willing to rely on market economics and plural democracy," he said. "That should give us a chance to improve our current credit rating."
Croatia is currently rated at the bottom of the investment grade ladder, carrying a Baa3 from Moody's and a BBB- from Standard & Poors.
"I have no doubt that the Croatian economy will get additional chances to get back on the track of economic recovery and that overall economic performance will improve," the minister added.
The country made its debut on the Eurobond market earlier this year with a $250 million issue and plans a further issue, denominated in German marks, in the second half of this year.
